‘Ramayana: Part 1’: Decoding the film’s massive budget and box-office performance
 As of today (November 16, 2026), ‘Ramayana: Part 1’, starring Yash, Ranbir Kapoor and Sai Pallavi, has raked in ₹1,384.50 crore (worldwide gross) in 12 days with its India net collection being ₹769.55 crore, as per Sacnilk
 Published - November 16, 2026 04:17 pm IST 
 The Hindu Bureau READ LATER 
 SEE ALL 
 Remove 
 Ranbir Kapoor in ‘Ramayana: Part 1’
 | Photo Credit: Special Arrangement
 It has been more than 10 days since the release of Nitesh Tiwari’s mythological epic, Ramayana: Part 1 . While the film is sparking conversations about its monumental scale and portrayal of specific instances from the epic, discussions are also focusing on its budget and box-office performance.
 According to industry tracker Sacnilk, Ramayana: Part 1 crossed ₹1000 crore (gross) at the global box office. It became the 11 th Indian film to do so, after Tiwari’s Dangal , Dhurandhar: The Revenge , Baahubali 2 , Pushpa 2: The Rule, and Dhurandhar, which are among the top five highest grossing films of all time.
 ALSO WATCH Ramayana: How Yash mastered the art of playing Ravana 
 As of today (November 16, 2026), Ramayana: Part 1 has raked in ₹1,384.50 crore (worldwide gross) in 12 days, with its India net collection being ₹769.55 crore, as per Sacnilk.
 With Ranbir Kapoor, Sai Pallavi, and Yash in the lead, Ramayana: Part 1 details events from the epic, showing Ravana’s (Yash) rise as the powerful king of Asuras. It also introduces Rama as a sensitive warrior who marries Sita (Sai Pallavi) and gets exiled to the forest for fourteen years. The film’s climactic sequence, involving a fight between the demigod Jatayu (voiced by Anupam Kher) and Ravana, has been praised for its craft and imagination.
 Ramayana: Part 1 is reportedly made on a budget of ₹2000 crore. The film’s whopping budget has been a point of discussion since its first look came out last year, and producer Namit Malhotra claimed in an interview that the two-part epic costs ₹4,000 crore. When the film’s trailer came out, it was met with criticisms particularly for its VFX and many viewers questioned claims about the mammoth budget. After the release, however, all apprehensions regarding the VFX have got cleared.
 Yash, whose banner Monster Mind Creations has co-produced the mythological epic, opened up on the budget during a pre-release promotional event in Bengaluru on October 15, 2026. He supported Namit’s statement and said, “In India, there is a problem. People don’t like it when you talk confidently. That’s what happened with Namit’s statement. But in the West, it’s the total opposite. If you tell them humbly that we have made a good movie, they will dismiss it as a small project. That’s exactly why Namit has confidently said that this movie is mounted on ₹4000 crore. We need to prove the strength of the Indian film industry to the global market,” Yash explained.
 The film’s box-office performance will give some respite to Yash after his last outing as an actor-producer, Toxic proved to be a major failure at the box-office.
 ‘Ramayana: Part 1’: Ranbir Kapoor’s earnest appeal gives new life to Rama Meanwhile, filmmaker Ram Gopal Varma took to X on November 15 to praise the film, calling it the “biggest hit ever in cinematic history.” He delved into the debate around the movie’s budget. He wrote, “I got to know that the actual cost of Part 1 is a little less than 800 and that includes mutually beneficial deals, global tax benefits, subsidy elements, which will eventually bring the cost to less than that. And not only me, but any reasonably experienced filmmaker, by seeing the film, can see the cost can’t be more than that.”
 Even for the best of my films she din't do this , but my mother has been buying tickets of @malhotra_namit 's #Ramayana for the servants , watch men etc in the building complex she lives , and inspite of this kind of euphoria leading it to breaking all box office records and fast emerging as the BIGGEST HIT EVER in INDIAN CINEMATIC HISTORY, stil lot of noise is being made by many jealous that the collections are still not enough because it's 2000 cr a piece making it 4000 for 2 
I got to know that the actual cost of part 1 is a little less than 800 and that includes mutually beneficial deals , global tax benefits , subsidy elements etc etc which all will eventually bring the cost to lesser than that .. And not only me but any reasonably experienced film maker by seeing the film can see the cost can't be more than that ..
Also many are stupid to assume that both parts will cost same ..That's like thinking the cost before interval and post interval will be same in a film ..I know of films where 50% of the cost was just climax 
Also much of the cost will include costs of creating the world of Ramayana which becomes future assets for gaming and various other aspects including assets for part 2 , which are all a part of Namit's visionary future outings .. And this part I frankly think , can't even be understood by most Bollywood makers , traders and other self proclaimed experts 
So going by how it's bull running now , it is obvious that Namit Malhotra is going to cover the entire cost of part 1 or maybe both parts in part 1 itself and then there's the non theatrical of part 1 and all revenue inflows of part 2 
So in other words Namit Malhotra can build his own Pushpak vimaan and start dumping money into innumerable extraordinary ventures which all the biggest production companies from north to south couldn't do till now and then he can surpass even the biggest of the biggest Hollywood biggies 
I don't know what happened to Valmiki Ji or Tulsidas ji after they did their work , but it's an irrefutable fact that , from now onwards Namit Malhotra will be the biggest mega film maker in history since 1913's May 3rd release Raja Harishchandra , till whichever the biggest film came before November 5 th 2026 ..If anyone has a doubt just do the math 
And the fact that the most fantastic action set pieces will be in part 2 starting from the Hanuman acts , Vaanar Sena , Ram Sethu , Lanka dhahanam , Sita in Lanka , Kumbha Karan's death , Ravan vadh and many many more just to name a few , and going by the extraordinary proven Vision of Namit Malhotra's combination of strategy , business acumen , creative understanding and visionary outlook, If KGF 2 did around 5 times more than KGF 1 , I am convinced that Ramayana 2 will do 10 times more than Ramayana part 1 ..If you disagree , we will talk in 2028
— Ram Gopal Varma (@RGVzoomin) November 15, 2026 He added, “Also, much of the cost will include the costs of creating the world of Ramayana, which will become future assets for gaming and various other aspects, including assets for part 2, which are all a part of Namit’s visionary future outings. And this part I frankly think, can’t even be understood by most Bollywood makers, traders and other self proclaimed experts.”
 It remains to be seen how the film progresses at the box office as anticipation builds for the second part, which will cover the rest of the story, bringing in Hanuman, played by Sunny Deol, and a host of other characters, as Rama takes the next steps to rescue Sita from Ravana’s Lanka. The second part will be released in theatres in 2028.
